### Agent Name: Planner  
### Step Number: 1  
### Reason for Mistake: The Planner prematurely concluded that 1999 was the promo year based on initial retrieved data from Wikipedia without sufficiently verifying discrepancies or extending the search to cross-validate with additional credible sources. While the Wikipedia output correctly denoted “1999” as the release year of Guns N’ Roses’ song “Oh My God” on the *End of Days* soundtrack, Planner conflated the release date of the movie and soundtrack with the year of promotional activity occurring on radio channels, which extended prominently into 2000. This oversight led to an incorrect assumption that all promo activity was confined to 1999, rather than synthesizing evidence indicating broader exposure spanning into 2000.  

The Planner failed to adapt its approach or refine understanding based on recurring hints identified later by WebSurfer regarding the Billboard exposure extending into early 2000. Instead, Planner persisted on asserting 1999 as the definitive year, demonstrating misinterpretation of chronological promo timelines. Thus, the Planner failed to synthesize temporal evidence systematically, leading to an inaccurate conclusion.
